data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A decentralized network of small services is less resilient to correlated failure than one large service with strictly more total internal redundancy, because the large service can enforce heterogeneous isolation (diverse OS kernels, compilers, power grids) by fiat, whereas decentralized nodes inevitably converge on hidden monocultures.","counterconditions":[{"case":"Decentralized nodes do not exhibit homophily and naturally adopt heterogeneous dependencies.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The large service's internal governance fails to prevent isomorphic dependency creep across its internal redundancy domains.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The shared causes affecting decentralized nodes are strictly localized and do not propagate across the network.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Independence must be engineered and enforced. A large centralized service has the governance power to mandate disjoint dependencies across its internal redundancy domains. A decentralized network lacks this enforcement mechanism; independent operators rationally adopt the same widely-trusted dependencies (e.g., the same cloud provider, the same TLS library, the same NTP servers) to minimize costs, creating latent correlated failure modes that are invisible until a shared cause triggers them.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
